column1: # 3장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명(장면 끝까지 모든 요청에 붙는다).

column2: At breakfast on Yuna's third day, Montse puts a shopping list and a twenty-euro note on the table and sends her to the market alone, so that she will learn. Montse is kind but does not go easy on her.
simple and firm, handing over the list
surprised, a little alarmed: me, alone?

At the Mercat de la Llibertat, a friendly fruit seller calls Yuna "guapa" and asks "¿qué te pongo?" (what can I get you). Yuna shops with "quiero" and the numbers she wrote down the night before; the seller reads the long word "melocotones" aloud for her, and Yuna learns "cuánto es" and "cincuenta". Busy and warm, a small victory.
careful, a beginner, trying the new word
reading the long word aloud for her, helpfully
careful, saying a number she memorized
careful, a beginner, proud of the question

At the cheese stall there is no queue; an old woman teaches Yuna to ask "¿Quién es el último?" (who's last?) to find her place. A tall, unsmiling man, Marc, answers "Yo". Yuna can't say "200 grams"; Marc orders for her in Catalan, then teaches her "doscientos" (dos + cien) word by word. He recognizes Montse's handwriting on her list, says Montse is his great-aunt, looks a long time at Yuna's grandmother's key, and gives nothing away. Marc is dry and curt; Yuna is curious and flustered.
helpful, slow, teaching the phrase to a foreigner
curt, in Catalan, to the seller
teaching the number slowly, word by word, dry; stress "dos" and "cien"
repeating the number she just learned, careful
a curt nod of approval: that's it
pleased with herself, trying the Catalan goodbye

column1: Esta letra… es de la Montse.
Es mi tía. Bueno… tía abuela.

column2: holding out the key, heart racing, hopeful
flat; impossible to tell whether he is joking

Back at the boarding house, Montse counts Yuna's change and praises her. When Yuna mentions meeting Marc and imitates his deadpan "Una llave", "No sé", Montse makes a sound between a laugh and a sigh and says no more. The scene ends with Yuna remembering a tiny flower on Marc's watch. Warm, then quietly mysterious.
counting the change aloud, then pleased
half a laugh, half a sigh
